name: Primary Immunodeficiency with Post-Measles-Mumps-Rubella Vaccine Viral Infection
aliases: PID with MMR Vaccine-Associated Viral Infection

criteria.description: Documented severe or disseminated viral infection following MMR vaccination
Laboratory evidence of impaired cellular and/or humoral immunity consistent with primary immunodeficiency
Exclusion of secondary causes of immunodeficiency such as HIV infection or immunosuppressive therapy
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with primary immunodeficiency (if available)
Improvement of clinical course with immunoglobulin replacement therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of documented severe viral infection post-MMR vaccine plus laboratory evidence of primary immunodeficiency with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and laboratory based; genetic confirmation may aid but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe systemic infection caused by vaccine strain measles virus
searchTerms: widespread measles infection from vaccine strain
severe measles virus infection after vaccination

pathognomonic.notes: Chronic or recurrent infection with vaccine strain mumps virus
searchTerms: ongoing mumps infection from vaccine strain

common.notes: Frequent bacterial or viral infections of upper and lower airways
Poor growth and weight gain in infants and young children
Persistent diarrhea due to viral or opportunistic infections
Enlarged lymph nodes due to chronic immune activation

occasional.notes: Fungal infection of the oral mucosa
Enlargement of liver and spleen due to immune dysregulation
Persistent viral skin lesions such as warts or molluscum contagiosum
searchTerms: persistent skin infections caused by viruses

occasional.symptomName: Neurological manifestations secondary to viral encephalitis
occasional.notes: Seizures, altered consciousness due to viral CNS infection
searchTerms: brain symptoms from viral brain infection
nerve issues due to viral brain inflammation

rare.notes: Structural lung damage from recurrent infections
searchTerms: chronic lung damage with airway widening

rare.notes: Rare disseminated infection with rubella vaccine strain
searchTerms: severe rubella infection from vaccine strain
intense rubella virus illness after vaccination

laboratory: Low or absent serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, and/or IgM)
Lymphopenia or abnormal lymphocyte subsets (e.g., low CD4+ T cells)
Detection of vaccine-strain measles, mumps, or rubella virus by PCR in blood or tissues
imaging: Chest radiograph showing recurrent or chronic pulmonary infections
CT scan demonstrating bronchiectasis in chronic lung disease
other: Positive response to immunoglobulin replacement therapy
Exclusion of HIV and other secondary immunodeficiencies

distinguishingFeatures: Profound T and B cell deficiency from birth
Severe infections including opportunistic pathogens unrelated to vaccination
Usually fatal without early bone marrow transplantation
History of HIV exposure or risk factors

redFlags: Severe or disseminated viral infection following MMR vaccination
Failure to thrive with recurrent infections in infancy
references: Orange JS, et al. Primary Immunodeficiency Diseases: A Molecular and Genetic Approach. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.
Notarangelo LD. Primary Immunodeficiencies. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010.
Orphanet Report Series: Primary immunodeficiency with post-measles-mumps-rubella vaccine viral infection, ORPHA:431166
